reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about selective Cu oxidation and grain refinement in FeNiCrCoCu coatings, but the cited evidence does not directly support these premises. E1 and E2 describe oxide formation (Cr2O3, Fe2O3, and mixed spinels) in a different HEA (Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20) at 800°C, with no mention of selective Cu segregation or a Cu-rich oxide layer. E3 discusses grain refinement in a different alloy (CoCrFeNiMn) via cold spray, not thermal pre-treatment of FeNiCrCoCu. The key premises are thus largely unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Thermal pre-treatment of FeNiCrCoCu coating can induce selective Cu segregation and oxidation to form a Cu-rich oxide layer
Thermal pre-treatment can refine the grain structure of the coating
A Cu-rich oxide layer reduces direct metal-metal contact and oxidation-induced degradation during high-temperature wear
Grain refinement increases hardness and resistance to crack initiation, improving wear performance
The combined microstructural modifications synergistically improve high-temperature wear resistance
